h: Monks, a scandal and a cracking view
p: Fountains Abbey was founded in 1132 by a group of monks who left St Mary's Abbey in York in search of a simpler, stricter life. They joined the Cistercian order, and over the next four centuries the abbey grew into one of the richest in England. It all came to an end in 1539, when Henry VIII dissolved the monasteries.

The water garden has a juicy backstory too. It was laid out by John Aislabie, who had been Chancellor of the Exchequer until he was disgraced in the South Sea Bubble financial scandal. He retreated to his Yorkshire estate and poured his energy into creating a garden instead, and his son William later bought the abbey ruins to add to the view.

Don't miss Fountains Hall, a Jacobean mansion built partly with stone taken from the abbey, or St Mary's Church, a richly decorated Victorian church designed by William Burges in the deer park. For the classic view, head to Anne Boleyn's Seat, where the trees open up to reveal the abbey ruins in the distance.
Allow a full day, as the site is huge and the walks between the different areas are part of the fun. Wear comfortable shoes and bring a picnic if the weather's good.

Afterwards, head into Ripon, one of England's smallest cities. Its cathedral is well worth a look, and every evening at 9pm the Hornblower sets the watch in the market square, a tradition said to go back over a thousand years.
